First of all, I would like to thank UNCCD and Business for Land Platform, the G20 Global Land Initiative, and of course, the Government of Mongolia for convening this important discussion. It's a big opportunity for me to participate in this dialogue. because Spain fully welcomes this initiative because it reflects a fundamental idea. The future of mining cannot be measured only by the minerals we extract, but by the landscape we restore, the communities we strengthen, and the opportunities we create during mining activities and after mining. activities. In other words, a land positive mining. For many decades, mining has been an essential driver for economic development and now is essential for energy transition. However, this transition only can be sustainable if is accompanying equally with ambitious objectives to restore ecosystem, recover biodiversity and improve people life. I would like to share with you two Spanish initiatives that have been awarded by international organizations. The first of them is in the framework of the just transition strategy in Spain with the European Recovery Funds. Spain launched one of Europe's largest public investment in ecological restoration of former coal mining areas. More than 105 million 50 million, sorry, have been mobilized to restore the great landscape in Spain. More than 2,200 hectares of former mining land, while creating hundreds of quality work, of quality jobs, with priority given to former coal miners and workers in auxiliary companies. But these projects are much more than restoring land. They are restoring water systems, removing polluted sediments and protecting aquifers. They are restoring ecosystems, planting more than one million native trees and shrubs for the recovery of grasslands, forests and wildlife habitats. And they are improving also public safety, sealing abandoned mine entrances and removing hazardous wastes. And very important, they are restoring economic opportunities by supporting sustainable forestry, extensive livestock farming, rural tourism, and new local businesses. In short, restoration is becoming a new driver for territorial development. This initiative has been recognized by the International Labour Organization as a good practice in delivering a just transition that protects both workers and community, recognizing that the most inspiring aspect of this experience is that the people who once extracted coal now are restoring nature. And this demonstrates that ecological restoration is not only an environmental policy, It's an investment in people. It creates skilled employment. It strengthens rural communities and reinforces social cohesion. And the second initiative I wanted to share with you is an initiative in the framework of the largest European saltwater lagoon. It's called Mar Menor, it's in the southeast of Spain. and it has long-term and severe environmental degradation caused by heavy metals residues from abandoned mining activities in their basin. The initiative is through an integrated restoration strategy combining tailings sealing, phytoremediation and biological restoration. Spain is working to recover this unique ecosystem.
